q: Which luminaire will you use to highlight (floodlight) a building facade?
n: Floodlights throw a broad, intense beam to wash a facade, so they are used to highlight buildings at night. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (Exterior/Floodlighting); Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Lighting).

q: Which lighting unit has built-in batteries?
n: Emergency lighting units have built-in rechargeable batteries that switch on automatically when normal power fails. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR, Div. 10.2.5 (Emergency Lighting); PEC Part 1, Art. 7.0.

q: Which luminaire is used as accent light?
n: Track or spot lights give a concentrated, adjustable beam that emphasizes objects, artwork or features. That is accent lighting. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (Accent Lighting); Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: The highly reflective interior surface commonly found in troffer luminaires and used to improve lighting efficiency and light distribution is typically fabricated from which material?
n: Troffer reflectors are usually anodized aluminum, which is highly reflective, light and corrosion-resistant. Source: IES Lighting Handbook, 10th ed. (luminaire materials).

q: In an IP rating, what does the first digit indicate?
o: Maximum operating temperature of the equipment
Degree of protection against solid objects and dust
Degree of protection against water ingress
n: In an IP (Ingress Protection) rating such as IP65, the first digit (0–6) rates protection against solid objects and dust. 6 means dust-tight. Source: IEC 60529.

q: In an IP rating, what does the second digit indicate?
o: Degree of protection against water ingress
Degree of protection against solid objects and dust
Maximum operating voltage of the equipment
Resistance to corrosion and ultraviolet radiation
n: In an IP (Ingress Protection) rating, the second digit rates protection against water, from 0 (none) up to 9 (high-pressure, high-temperature jets). For example, 7 means temporary immersion. Source: IEC 60529.

q: Manufacturers of lighting fixtures, CCTV cameras, electrical enclosures, and other building equipment commonly indicate an IP rating in their technical specifications. What is the primary purpose of an IP rating?
o: To identify the operating voltage and current requirements of a device
To classify the energy efficiency of an electrical device
To indicate the degree of protection provided against the intrusion of solid objects and water
To determine the illumination output and service life of a lighting fixture
n: An IP (Ingress Protection) rating shows how well an enclosure keeps out solid objects and water. Source: IEC 60529.

q: A lighting fixture is specified for installation on the exterior facade of a proposed building. The fixture is expected to be exposed to dust, heavy rain, and periodic cleaning using water jets. Which IP rating would most appropriately satisfy these requirements?
n: IP65 means dust-tight (6) and protected against water jets (5). That covers dust, heavy rain and hose cleaning. Source: IEC 60529.

q: A kind of lighting designed for both indoor and outdoor applications. Also known as tape or ribbon lights, it is very flexible and can-be easily cut into the desired length.
n: Strip (tape or ribbon) lights are flexible LED strips that can be cut to length, for indoor or outdoor use. Source: IES Lighting Handbook, 10th ed. (linear LED products).

q: Which type of lighting is most commonly used for emergency signage due to its high visibility, low power consumption, and long operational life during battery-backup mode?
n: Emergency and exit signs mostly use LEDs: highly visible, low power and long-lasting on battery backup. Source: NFPA 101, Sec. 7.10; UL 924.

q: What do you call the device used in LED lighting that converts and regulates the power supplied to the LEDs?
n: An LED driver supplies regulated (usually constant-current) DC power to LEDs. It is the counterpart of a ballast for discharge lamps. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (LED Sources and Drivers); Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings.

q: Which device is used to automatically turn lighting on and off?
n: An occupancy (motion) sensor turns lighting on when it detects people and off after the space is vacated. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (Lighting Controls); Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Energy Efficiency – Lighting Controls.

q: How many physical switches are required to operate a standard 3-way switching setup as per NEC and CEC standards?
n: A three-way setup controls one light from two locations using two three-way switches. Source: NEC/Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) 2017, Part 1, Art. 4.4 (switches); Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (MEEB).

q: Which device is designed to allow building occupants to manually activate the fire alarm system in case of an emergency?
n: A manual pull station lets occupants trigger the fire alarm by hand. Source: NFPA 72, Sec. 17.14 (Manually Actuated Alarm-Initiating Devices); RIRR of RA 9514.

q: A computer-based control system that centrally controls and monitors the building systems.
n: A Building Management System is a computer-based system that centrally controls and monitors building services. Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB (building automation); ASHRAE Guideline 13.

q: Which of the following technologies is specifically designed as a communication protocol for building automation and control networks, including HVAC, lighting, and fire safety systems?
n: BACnet (ASHRAE/ANSI 135, ISO 16484-5) is the communication protocol for building automation networks such as HVAC, lighting and fire systems. Source: ASHRAE Standard 135.

q: Which of the following technologies is primarily used to establish a wired communication network within a building, enabling data exchange between computers, servers, and building automation devices?
n: A Local Area Network (LAN) is the wired network linking computers, servers and automation devices within a building. Source: ANSI/TIA-568 (structured cabling).

q: A modern high-rise building integrates its air-conditioning, lighting, energy monitoring, elevators, access control, and alarm systems into a centralized platform that allows facility managers to monitor performance, receive notifications, analyze energy consumption, and remotely control building operations from a single interface. What system performs this function?
n: A Building Management System brings HVAC, lighting, energy monitoring, elevators, access and alarms onto one platform for monitoring and control. Source: ASHRAE Guideline 13; Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: What is a self-contained surveillance system comprising cameras, recorders and displays for monitoring activities?
n: Closed-circuit television (CCTV) is a self-contained surveillance system of cameras, recorders and monitors. Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB (security systems).

q: In an intercom system, which station can control the entire system?
n: In an intercom system the master station can call and control all other stations. Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB (intercommunication systems).

q: Which among the following is a recognized brand associated with electronic security systems, specifically intrusion alarms and wireless security devices?
n: Visonic is a security brand known for intrusion alarms and wireless sensors. Cisco is networking, Phelps Dodge is wire, Delta is power electronics. Source: Manufacturer product lines.

q: In the context of building auxiliary and security systems, what does IDS stand for?
n: IDS stands for Intrusion Detection System. It detects unauthorized entry. Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB (security systems); ASIS International glossary.

q: Which device is used to absorb the shock when water flowing in a pipe suddenly stops due to fast-closing shutoff valves? It is also known as an air chamber.
n: A water hammer arrester (air chamber or shock absorber) cushions the pressure surge when flowing water is stopped suddenly by a fast-closing valve. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Sec. 609 (Water Hammer); Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings.

q: Which is an underground valve used to join a service pipe to a street water main?
n: A corporation stop (corporation cock) is the underground valve tapped into the street water main where the service pipe is joined. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Definitions; Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (Water Service).

q: Which is a water service shutoff valve located between the water main and the building, usually found under the sidewalk, and operated by a key?
n: A curb stop (curb cock) is the shutoff valve on the service line between the main and the building. It usually sits under the sidewalk in a curb box and is operated with a key. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Definitions; Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings.

q: An unobstructed vertical clearance through the free atmosphere between the lowest opening from any pipe of faucet conveying potable water to the flood-level rim of any tank, vat or fixture
n: The water-distribution air gap is the unobstructed vertical space between the lowest potable-water outlet and the flood-level rim of the fixture or tank. It prevents backflow. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Definitions (Air Gap, Water Distribution).

q: Which of the following residential spaces is specifically designed to generate high levels of heat and steam, often using heated elements or stones, and is intended for dry or moist therapeutic exposure?
n: A sauna uses heated elements or stones to produce high heat and steam for dry or moist therapy. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated; ASHRAE (sauna design).

q: A pump used to move water vertically from the underground cistern up to the overhead tank.
n: A transfer pump lifts water from the underground cistern to the overhead tank. Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB (water supply systems).

q: A pump which uses an impeller and volute to move fluid by the conversion of rotational kinetic energy to hydrodynamic energy. It has varied applications, one of which is to move water to an elevated water tank.
n: A centrifugal pump uses an impeller and volute, converting rotational kinetic energy into hydrodynamic energy. It is widely used to lift water to elevated tanks. Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB; Karassik, Pump Handbook.

q: A pump suitable for clear water transfer. It is commonly used for draining water tanks, removing water from the basements of construction sites, etc.
n: Transfer pumps move clear water from place to place, such as draining tanks or dewatering basements on construction sites. Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: A pump used at the elevator pit.
n: A sump pump in the elevator pit removes water that collects there. Source: ASME A17.1 (pit drainage); Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: A pump designed to increase the pressure in a pipeline to the desired level when there is inadequate pressure.
n: A booster pump raises pipeline pressure where the supply pressure is inadequate. Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: A pump connected to the fire sprinkler system to maintain pressure in the sprinkler pipes.
n: A jockey pump keeps the sprinkler or standpipe piping pressurized and makes up small losses, so the main fire pump does not start needlessly. Source: NFPA 20 (Pressure Maintenance Pumps).

q: Which has a built-in trap?
n: Water closets have a built-in (integral) trap. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 10 (Traps).

q: Which plumbing fixture does not require a separate external S-trap or P-trap, because its trap seal is already integrated into the fixture's hydraulic design, making any additional trap a prohibited double-trapping condition?
n: A water closet's trap is part of the fixture. Adding another trap would make a prohibited double trap. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 10 (fixtures with integral traps; double trapping prohibited).

q: This type of trap is sleek-looking and became popular in small or compact bathrooms, especially in Europe. It needs to be fitted correctly, otherwise it would not be efficient. The flow is not very efficient and it is prone to clogging.
n: Bottle traps look sleek and suit compact bathrooms, but must be fitted correctly, flow less efficiently and clog easily. Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB (traps); EN 274.

q: During a forensic plumbing inspection of an older residential structure, the investigators note recurring sewer-gas odor despite the fixture being unused for several days. The trap arm shows no signs of evaporation, but the trap seal depth is consistently reduced after each discharge. The drain connection drops vertically into the floor with no accessible vent connection within the allowable developed length. Which type of trap configuration is most likely installed, given the observed self-siphonage and code-noncompliant geometry?
n: An S-trap drops straight into the floor with no vent within the allowed distance. It self-siphons and loses its seal after each discharge, which is why the code prohibits it. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 10 (prohibited traps: S-traps).

q: What do you call the flush tank of a water closet?
n: The water closet's flush tank is the toilet cistern. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Definitions; Stein & Reynolds, MEEB.

q: Which component in a commercial kitchen plumbing system is specifically designed to intercept FOG (Fats, Oils and Grease) before they enter the drainage system, preventing blockages and costly. repairs?
n: A grease trap (interceptor) captures fats, oils and grease (FOG) from kitchen waste before they reach the drainage system. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 10 (Grease Interceptors).

q: Under the National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, the minimum size of a sanitary drainage pipe is primarily determined by which factor?
o: Number of storeys served by the building
Water pressure available at the fixture
Total DFU connected to the pipe
n: Sanitary drain pipes are sized by the total drainage fixture units (DFU) they carry. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 7 (Size of Drainage Piping, Table 7-5).

q: A plumber is sizing the sanitary drainage system of a residential unit. Most plumbing fixtures are sized using the standard drainage-pipe sizing procedures prescribed by the National Plumbing Code of the Philippines. Which fixture typically requires compliance with a prescribed minimum drainage pipe size (exception to the rule) regardless of the sizing calculations used for other fixtures?
n: Water closets have a prescribed minimum drain size of 75 mm (3 in.), whatever the DFU calculation gives for other fixtures. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (RNPCP, 1999), Ch. 7 (minimum drain size for water closets).

q: A type of regulating valve commonly used to precisely control the flow of fluids or gases within a system. It features a slender and tapered stem.
n: A needle valve has a slender, tapered stem for precise control of fluid or gas flow. Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB (valves); ASME B16.34.

q: Which is not a regulating valve?
n: A check valve only prevents backflow. It does not throttle, so it is not a regulating valve. Diaphragm, ball and butterfly valves can regulate flow. Source: Stein & Reynolds, MEEB (valves).
